1.explanation:
1. plugins/file-highlight/prism-file-highlight.js – This hook fetches the external file and calls Prism.highlightElement on the loaded content, so any mis-tokenization in Prism’s core/grammar will manifest here when the file contains back-ticks.
2. components/prism-javascript.js – Defines the JavaScript grammar, including the `template-string` token that (too greedily) treats any back-tick sequence as a template literal and doesn’t respect comment contexts. This mis-parses back-ticks inside comments.
3. prism.js – Prism’s core highlighting engine that loads the above grammar and applies it via hooks. The core methods triggered by file-highlight (before-sanity-check, highlightElement, etc.) rely on the grammar in prism-javascript.js to correctly tokenize back-ticks, which currently they do not.
1.bug_scenario: The Prism site’s “highlight” demo on the homepage uses the File-Highlight plugin to fetch external JavaScript source files and then invokes Prism.highlightElement on each <code> block. One of the demo files contains JSDoc comments with back-ticks (e.g. in “`language-xxxx`”). The JavaScript grammar in Prism mis-interprets those back-ticks as template-string delimiters, causing it to eat the remainder of the code block and break highlighting downstream once you scroll far enough (around 90%).
